title: Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program Cost-Share Collection and the Medicare Monthly Insulin Cap
content:
The customer's cost share for a fill on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is what the plan's real-time pharmacy remittance shows, collected when the refill ships.

## Pricing rule

**1. By tier family.**
- On commercial tiers: the tier's copay per 30-day supply for each 30 days of supply of a preferred insulin (the tier's non-preferred copay per 30 days under an approved formulary exception), or the tier's coinsurance percent of the allowed amount on the PPO tier after its deductible.
- On the Medicaid tier: the nominal copay.
- On the self-pay tier: the item's Larkfield cash price.

**2. The Medicare monthly cap.** On tiers where the Medicare monthly insulin cap is greater than 0.00, the customer never pays more than that amount for each month's supply of each covered insulin product, with no deductible, so a 90-day fill of one insulin costs at most three times the cap; pen needles and syringes are not insulin and are not capped.

**3. Remittance above the cap.** When a remittance shows a patient responsibility above the cap for a covered insulin, Larkfield posts only the capped amount and reports the remittance to the plan as a pricing error; the difference is never billed to the customer.

## The capped amount, defined

On a tier with a cap above 0.00, the amount posted for a covered insulin on a fill is the lower of two figures: the patient responsibility on the remittance, which is the allowed amount less the amount the payer paid; and the monthly cap multiplied by the fill's supply days and divided by 30.

## Worked through (hypothetical remittances, cap of 35.00 per month)

| Fill | Allowed amount less payer paid | Cap multiplied by supply days, divided by 30 | Amount posted | Reported as pricing error? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| One insulin, 90 days | 300.00 less 180.00, which is 120.00 | 35.00 multiplied by 90, divided by 30, which is 105.00 | 105.00 | Yes; the 15.00 difference is never billed to the customer |
| One insulin, 30 days | 95.00 less 70.00, which is 25.00 | 35.00 | 25.00 | No |
| Pen needles, 90 days | 40.00 | Not capped — not insulin | 40.00 | No |

Each covered insulin product on a fill is capped on its own: two different insulins on one 30-day fill may each cost up to the monthly cap.
